newsitem.title: USA: TU Electric to offer refund, rate freeze.
newsitem.headline: TU Electric to offer refund, rate freeze.

text.p: TU Electric, a unit of Texas Utilities Co, said on Wednesday that it filed a proposal to refund $80 million to customers and freeze rates through the remainder of the year.

The proposal is the result of a joint agreement by TU Electric, the staff of the Public Utility Commission of Texas, the Office of the Public Utility Counsel and the Coalition of Cities Served by TU Electric, the company said.
TU Electric said it would make a one-time refund to customers in August 1997 as a credit on their bills.
TU Electric said a typical residential customer would receive a refund of $17.
The proposal is pending approval from the Public Utility Commission of Texas, TU Electric said.

The Public Utility Commission's staff reviewed TU Electric's earnings last year and found that they are potentially higher than would be allowed if the company underwent a rate case, TU Electric said.

TU Electric said the commission's staff did not include the effects of a Texas Supreme Court ruling that directed the commission to reconsider a $909 million disallowance from the company's 1990 rate case.
The ruling could lead to an increase in the amount that TU Electric is allowed to earn, TU Electric said.
The refund proposal will enable the company and the state to negotiate a longer-term resolution of the company's earnings beyond 1997, which would address the court ruling, TU Electric said.
